chunk_findings.detail: `curl-user` only matches a standalone `-u`/`--user` after whitespace, then requires `[ =]+` before the user. chunk_findings.detail: The JWT shape requires two `eyJ` segments and a third segment of `[0-9A-Za-z_-]{8,}` with no `=`. chunk_findings.detail: The unchanged-name branch also requires `len(safe) <= _STEM_KEEP`, so a previously valid agent id that `safe_filename` leaves alone but is 49–128 characters long is moved to a digest shard. For example, with `agent_id = "a" * 49`, `safe_filename` leaves the id alone and the old `EventLog.shard` path was `"a" * 49 + ".jsonl"`, but after this change the path becomes `"a" * 48 + "~" + digest + ".jsonl"`. A log written before the change is therefore no longer found by the new `shard` path (and not included in the agent’s new shard), splitting or losing the agent’s history despite the stated goal of keeping names unchanged for ids the filename filter leaves alone.

chunk_findings.detail: The exemption justifies a 128-character agent id by saying the file system name limit is 255 bytes and that characters may take four bytes, but 128 × 4 bytes already exceeds 255 before the digest suffix and `.jsonl` are added. The boundary test in `tests/test_agent_id.py:42` reinforces the wrong assumption by using `"é" * 100` (200 bytes plus suffix) while calling it “at the cap,” not `"é" * 128` (256 bytes plus suffix) or a 128-character four-byte id such as `"\U0001F600" * 128`. If the validator enforces only the stated 128-character/no-control-character rule and the sanitizer leaves such non-control characters in the readable shard name, that id is accepted and the shard name is over 255 bytes, producing the file-system `OSError` the change is supposed to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: For an agent id that `safe_filename` leaves unchanged but is longer than `_STEM_KEEP`, `shard_stem` does not keep the old shard name. Input `agent_id = "a" * 50` is accepted by `agent_id_problem`, contains no control character, and is far below the 255-byte filesystem limit, but `len(safe) <= _STEM_KEEP` is false, so `shard_stem` returns `"a" * 48 + "~" + digest(...)` instead of `"a" * 50`. The previous code would have used `"a" * 50 + ".jsonl"`, so an existing log shard for that agent id is orphaned after the change, contrary to the stated replay-compatibility requirement for ids the filter leaves alone.

chunk_findings.detail: `_UNSAFE = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f]")` only rejects ASCII C0 controls and DEL, not other Unicode control characters. Given `agent_id = "foo\u0085bar"` (U+0085 NEXT LINE, a Unicode `Cc` control character and line separator), `agent_id_problem` returns `""`, and `EventLog` constructs successfully instead of refusing the id. The change’s validation contract is “no control characters,” but this hostile id is accepted; if `safe_filename` does not strip it, it can also remain in the shard name.

chunk_findings.detail: The unchanged-name branch still drops previously valid shard names. `_NAME_BYTES = 240` is not the maximum stem length allowed by the stated 255-byte file-name limit plus `.jsonl` (that would be 249 bytes), so a previously writable log can move to a digest shard. For example, with `agent_id = "é" * 121` (121 characters, 242 UTF-8 bytes, no control characters), the old `EventLog.shard` path was `"é" * 121 + ".jsonl"` (248 bytes total, valid under the usual 255-byte component limit). After this change, `shard_stem` fails `len(safe.encode()) <= _NAME_BYTES` and returns a `~digest` name, so a log written before the change is no longer found by `EventLog.shard`, contradicting the docstring’s “replays under the same file” claim and r-replay-compat.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:_NAME_BYTES

chunk_findings.detail: The added `AGENT_ID_MAX` exemption still treats the id cap as if it guarantees a safe file-system name, but the cap is documented as a bound on the id itself while the actual file-name limit is a byte limit. With a 128-character id made of four-byte UTF-8 characters, e.g. `agent_id = "\U0001F600" * 128`, the id is within a 128-character cap, yet its UTF-8 encoding is 512 bytes; after adding `.jsonl` the shard name is over 255 bytes and can reproduce the same `OSError` this change is supposed to prevent. The separate `_NAME_BYTES` exemption acknowledges the byte limit, but the `AGENT_ID_MAX` exemption does not tie validation or shard naming to UTF-8 byte length, so the documented cap still justifies an unsafe character-based limit.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.d/ddflow.core.ids.toml:2

chunk_findings.detail: The multi-byte “at the cap” case is `"é" * 100`, but the rest of the suite fixes the cap at 128 characters (`"a" * 128` is accepted, `"a" * 129` is refused, and the CLI test asserts `128`). So the test does not actually exercise the cap for multi-byte ids: a valid 128-character id such as `"\U0001F600" * 128` (or `"é" * 128`) has the same character length as the accepted ASCII case but can produce a shard name well over the 255-byte filesystem limit if non-ASCII ids are left as `safe_filename` leaves them. The test would still pass because it only checks a 200-byte id, so it fails to guard the original “valid capped id still gives OSError” class of regression. This is the previous boundary finding still unaddressed: the current test still uses 100 rather than `I.AGENT_ID_MAX` and adds no four-byte cap case.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_id.py:54

chunk_findings.detail: The unchanged-name branch keeps a shard only when `len(safe.encode()) <= _NAME_BYTES` (240), but a file-name component may be 255 bytes and `.jsonl` is 6, so stems of 241–249 bytes were legal before this change. Given `agent_id = "a" * 241`, `safe_filename` leaves it unchanged and the old `EventLog.shard` path was `"a" * 241 + ".jsonl"` (247 bytes). `shard_stem` now takes the digest branch and returns a different name, so that log is not replayed. The comment on `_NAME_BYTES` even states the limit as 255 minus 6, which is 249, not 240.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:_NAME_BYTES

chunk_findings.detail: The previous byte-limit objection still stands, and the new replay test makes it worse. `test_a_long_id_the_old_naming_accepted_keeps_its_shard_so_old_logs_replay` requires a 128-character id the sanitizer leaves unchanged to be stored as `{agent}.jsonl` with no shortening digest, while `test_an_id_at_the_cap_is_accepted_and_its_shard_name_fits_the_file_system` still treats `"é" * 100` (200 UTF-8 bytes) as the multi-byte cap and the overlong case only starts at `"é" * 130`. Given `agent_id = "é" * 128` (128 characters, 256 UTF-8 bytes) or `"\U0001F600" * 64` (under a 128-character cap, 256 bytes), validation that only checks character length accepts the id, the kept stem plus `.jsonl` exceeds Linux `NAME_MAX` (255 bytes), and `EventLog.append` still raises `OSError`. The suite never constructs that input, so it does not fail against the unfixed code.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_id.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: `_NAME_BYTES = 240` is below the largest old shard stem that could already have existed under a 255-byte filesystem component limit (255 minus `.jsonl` = 249), so an agent id that remains valid under the new validation can silently be given a new shard name and lose its old log. Given `agent_id = "漢" * 81`, `agent_id_problem` returns `""` (81 characters is within `AGENT_ID_MAX`, and the characters are not `Cc`/`Zl`/`Zp`); with `unicode=True`, `safe_filename` leaves these Unicode letters unchanged, but `len(safe.encode())` is `243`, so `shard_stem` takes the digest branch and returns `"漢" * 48 + "~" + digest + ".jsonl"`. The previous code produced `"漢" * 81 + ".jsonl"`, which is 249 bytes and therefore a valid old shard name, so an existing pre-change shard is not found by `shard`/`shards()` and does not replay [r-replay-compat]. The unchanged-name threshold should preserve all old safe stems that fit the filesystem limit (or reject them explicitly), not rename them at 240 bytes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:shard_stem

chunk_findings.detail: The new test treats `é`*100 as an id “at the cap” and accepted, while other tests require the CLI/`AGENT_ID_MAX` boundary to be `128`. But `é`*100 is 200 UTF-8 bytes, so if the cap is enforced in bytes (the only unit that matters for the 255-byte filename limit the bug is about), this test is wrong and will fail; if the cap is enforced in characters (as the test implies), then the actual boundary id `é`*128 is accepted but its shard name `é`*128 + `.jsonl` is 262 bytes, exceeding the 255-byte filesystem name limit and reproducing the original `OSError` on append. The parametrization only checks `é`*100 (206 bytes with `.jsonl`), so it does not validate the byte boundary needed by the fix.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_id.py:test_an_id_at_the_cap_is_accepted_and_its_shard_name_fits_the_file_system

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertions make the shard name for ids containing characters that `safe_filename` replaces differ from the old sanitized name: the old test expected `EventLog(..., "x:y").shard.name == "x_y.jsonl"`, while the new test expects it to start with `"x_y~"`. Given an existing log shard `x_y.jsonl` created by the previous code for agent id `x:y`, after this change `EventLog.shard` is `x_y~<digest>.jsonl`, so appends/replay use a new empty shard and the old events under `x_y.jsonl` are not replayed. The diff contains no migration/compat fallback in the visible change, and the test change itself codifies the replay break rather than preserving the old shard name, violating the stated `r-replay-compat` requirement.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier replay break is only partly fixed. `_NAME_BYTES` is 240, but a shard stem may be 249 bytes (255 minus `.jsonl`) and still be a name the previous `safe_filename(agent_id)+".jsonl"` path wrote. `agent_id = "é" * 121` is 121 characters (under `AGENT_ID_MAX`) and 242 UTF-8 bytes. If `safe_filename(..., unicode=True)` leaves it unchanged, `len(safe.encode()) <= _NAME_BYTES` is false, so `shard_stem` returns a 48-character prefix plus `~` and a digest instead of the old 121-character stem. That log no longer replays under the same file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:shard_stem

chunk_findings.detail: The added exemption states that `_NAME_BYTES` is “the longest shard file name a file system allows (255 bytes) less the `.jsonl` suffix” (i.e. 249 bytes) and that “an id within it keeps the name an older log was written under,” but the constant it exempts in `ddflow/core/ids.py` is still 240. Given `agent_id = "é" * 121` (121 characters, 242 UTF-8 bytes, within the 128-character id cap and left unchanged by `safe_filename`), the old shard name was `"é" * 121 + ".jsonl"`, 248 bytes and valid. `shard_stem` now compares `len(safe.encode())` against 240, takes the digest branch, and returns a different stem, so the pre-existing log under the original name is not replayed. This violates [r-replay-compat]; the docs do not fix the code and misstate the byte limit.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.d/ddflow.core.ids.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: [r-replay-compat] The new `shard_stem` preserves an old shard name only when `safe_filename(agent_id, repl="_", unicode=True)` is the identity. For any id that the previous code sanitized, the old shard name is not preserved. Example: with agent id `"x:y"`, the old code produced `x_y.jsonl`; the new code returns `x_y~<digest>.jsonl` because `safe != agent_id`. Thus an existing `.ddflow/events/x_y.jsonl` written by the old code for agent `"x:y"` is no longer the path returned by `EventLog(root, "x:y").shard`, so appends go to a new empty shard and any per-agent read/replay through `.shard` misses the old events. Raising `_NAME_BYTES` to 249 fixes the 240-byte case, but it does not make sanitized old logs replay under their old shard names.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ids.py:shard_stem

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertion `assert EventLog(adopted, "x:y").shard.name.startswith("x_y~")` (and the analogous `a b/c` assertion) makes any id whose old sanitizer rewrote characters use a different shard than it used before. The removed line `assert EventLog(adopted, "x:y").shard.name == "x_y.jsonl"` shows that an existing log for agent id `x:y` was at `x_y.jsonl`; after the change the same id resolves to `x_y~<digest>.jsonl`, so append/replay opens a new empty file and the old events are ignored. That violates the stated r-replay-compat requirement that old logs still replay under the new naming, and the test now enforces the break rather than a migration/fallback. [r-replay-compat]

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier replay break is still present: `_NAME_BYTES` is now 249, but injectivity is implemented by abandoning every old shard whose stem was `safe_filename(agent_id)`, not the raw id. Given an existing log `x_y.jsonl` written by the previous `safe_filename(..., repl="_", unicode=True)` path for agent id `x:y`, `safe != agent_id`, so `shard_stem` returns `x_y~<digest>` and `EventLog.shard` is `x_y~<digest>.jsonl`. Appends and replay open that new empty file; events still in `x_y.jsonl` are not read. The same split hits `a/b`, `a b`, and any other id the old filter rewrote. Nothing in this diff migrates or also reads the previous stem, so r-replay-compat still fails for those logs.

chunk_findings.detail: The replay break from the last review is still in the assertions this change keeps. `EventLog(..., "x:y").shard.name` is required to start with `x_y~`, and `EventLog(..., "a b/c").shard.name` with `a_b_c~`, instead of the previous `safe_filename` results `x_y.jsonl` and `a_b_c.jsonl`. chunk_findings.detail: Given an existing project whose agent id is `"a" * 200`, the old naming path accepted it: `safe_filename` returns the id unchanged and the shard name is `"a" * 200 + ".jsonl"`, 206 bytes, below the 255-byte component limit. After this change, `EventLog(root, "a" * 200)` calls `IDS.agent_id_problem`, which rejects every string longer than `AGENT_ID_MAX` (128) before `shard_stem` can preserve the old shard name. Thus the same previously usable agent id now raises `ValueError`, so its existing shard cannot be opened, replayed, or appended as that agent. This is a regression against [r-replay-compat] and contradicts the `_NAME_BYTES` comment that names the old rule could write should still map to themselves; the cap is too strict for safe ASCII ids that fit the filesystem name budget.
